comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company implemented cost reduction measures including a restructuring plan that reduced headcount by approximately 15%, incurred $171 million in restructure charges, and achieved estimated quarterly savings of $130 million through 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Broadcom (AVGO) and Micron (MU) incurred restructuring-related charges driven by cost reduction activities and employee severance, but the magnitude and context differ significantly. AVGO recognized $1,533 million in 2024, primarily due to the VMware Merger cost reductions, whereas MU recognized only $171 million in 2023 (the most recent restructuring data provided for MU) from its 2023 Restructure Plan. While both cite employee severance as a primary component, AVGO's charges are an order of magnitude larger and explicitly tied to a major acquisition integration, while MU's were part of a broader industry downturn response involving headcount reductions.

sentences.text: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million and $244 million in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The fiscal year 2024 charges primarily included employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger.
We incurred restructure charges of $171 million in 2023 primarily related to employee severance costs.

These measures included the 2023 Restructure Plan, as well as implementing productivity programs, suspension of our 2023 bonus, reductions in select product programs, lower discretionary spending, and cuts to 2023 executive salaries.

comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses increased in fiscal year 2024 due to employee growth and compensation increases; fiscal year 2023 included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies recognized significant non-operating or special charges in recent fiscal years, though the drivers were different. AVGO's 2024 charges ($1,533 million) were primarily employee termination costs from the VMware Merger, while NVDA's notable prior year charge (2023) was a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the Arm transaction. In the current comparable period (2024), NVDA did not report a similar restructuring charge, attributing expense growth to employee growth and compensation, contrasting with AVGO's high restructuring costs. Both disclosures highlight the impact of strategic transactions (Merger/Acquisition attempts) on their financial charges.

comparisons.peer_summary: Other expenses, consisting primarily of restructuring and restructuring-related charges, decreased to $179 million in fiscal 2024 from $862 million in fiscal 2023.

While the magnitude differs vastly (AVGO's being much larger due to the scale of the VMware deal), both companies use similar terminology and identify restructuring as a key component of their non-recurring or other expense disclosures in FY2024.
